title: Red Bull working to fix Verstappen's Vegas practice issues
excerpt:
Red Bull are working to resolve the balance issues that hampered Max Verstappen during a disrupted opening day of running at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with Technical Director Pierre Wache admitting the team have work to do ahead of Friday's action.

Wet conditions severely limited running during FP1 on Thursday, with no drivers setting a lap time, before a drying track allowed for more action in FP2. However, Verstappen endured a difficult second session, finishing 13th after reporting a lack of power and struggling with his car's handling.

Asked about the four-time World Champion's delayed appearance in FP2, Wache explained that Red Bull had initially opted to keep Verstappen in the garage while conditions remained wet.

"We didn't plan to run with him when it was full wet tyre conditions," he explained. "We wanted to check the systems on the car at the beginning, which is why he didn't run from the start.

"After the track dried, we decided to go out on the intermediates before the red flag, but then the red flag happened. We rushed to get him out, unfortunately.

Wache continued: "He had some issues with the energy management. It wasn't a massive issue in that respect, just getting the systems working together. After that, he had a massive issue with the balance, which we're trying to understand and fix for tomorrow."

With dry conditions expected for Friday's final practice and Qualifying sessions, Wache acknowledged that Thursday's running offered limited insight into Red Bull's potential performance across the remainder of the weekend.

"The conditions were very cold, and the tyres we use will be completely different tomorrow," he explained. "I think it will be a completely different day. We'll be very busy tomorrow afternoon, for sure. But it's difficult to predict anything at the moment."

There was a more encouraging showing on the other side of the garage, with team mate Isack Hadjar finishing fourth in FP2, behind George Russell, Pierre Gasly and Charles Leclerc.

"I'm happy, and he's quite happy with the car," Wache said of Hadjar's performance. "That's quite positive. In these conditions, having a car you can trust is quite good."

Hadjar was similarly positive about his prospects, drawing comparisons between the Las Vegas Strip Circuit and Baku.

"I have a good feeling about this track," he said. "This layout in general reminds me of Baku, where we did really well. Long straights, slow-speed corners, low grip. So only the temperature is a different topic. But yeah, let's see what we can do."

title: Russell admits Mercedes lacking pace despite topping FP2
excerpt:
George Russell admits that "realistically we probably were not the fastest", despite finishing top of the times in a wet Free Practice 2 ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver finished less than one-tenth clear of Pierre Gasly's Alpine during Thursday's second, one-hour session on the streets of Las Vegas, which was held in wet but drying conditions.

Russell's time, a 1m 47.272s, came in the best of the conditions and just as the chequered flag was shown to end proceedings, with the likes of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris having been towards the top of the times all afternoon.

"We know in the wet that it's different every single lap, every single session you do," said Russell reflecting on his session.

"I think realistically we probably were not the fastest today. McLaren looked exceptionally fast, Charles looked very fast at points, we just got the lap in when the track was at its driest and Norris didn't run.

"We've got some things to understand because we were very competitive in the wet last week [in Brazil] and both Kimi [Antonelli] and I were off the pace [today]."

Thursday's second session was the only meaningful running drivers and teams got during the day and, with Friday set to be dry, Russell stated Free Practice 3 would be crucial in order to get a better understanding of how the tyres will perform in the cold conditions.

"I think nobody knows how the graining is going to be for Sunday," he said. "Last year was an easy one-stop but the year before there was lots of graining and it was a two-stop.

"So they're questions that we want answered but we probably won't get an answer until race day."

Ahead of the weekend, Russell opted against using a new turbo that Mercedes have introduced, but it will be used by team mate and World Champion, Kimi Antonelli.

As well as the new turbo, Antonelli’s Mercedes – which finished FP2 in P8 – has been fitted with a new internal combustion engine (ICE), his sixth of the season and surpassing the permitted number of four, meaning he will serve a five-place grid penalty.

"It's a very small performance gain in the sort of tens of milliseconds," said Mercedes Deputy Team Principal, Bradley Lord, when speaking about the new turbo.

"But we'll need to wait to get running in the dry to really see the full benefit and the full understanding of performance it brings and how it might improve some of the drivability of the PU."

title: Piastri shares early impressions of new engine in Las Vegas
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri has given his first impressions of the new power unit components onboard his McLaren after the opening day on track at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with the Australian expecting an “interesting” Qualifying as he prepares to serve a grid penalty.

It was confirmed prior to the event that Piastri will receive a 10-place grid drop due to a new internal combustion engine (ICE) being fitted in his MCL40, exceeding the allowance of four per season.

Both Piastri and team mate Lando Norris are also running a new turbocharger, with power unit supplier Mercedes bringing an upgrade via the Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) mechanism.

While heavy rain limited running during Thursday’s first practice session, the conditions had improved enough for the field to gain more laps in Free Practice 2 and Piastri ended the hour in P5 on the timesheets, two positions ahead of Norris.

The 25-year-old admitted that the running was “definitely not super relevant for the rest of the weekend” – in which drier conditions are expected – but spoke positively about the mileage he had been able to achieve.

“I think, obviously, on my side, we wanted to prove out the new engine we've got in and the new turbo as well, so [it was] good to get some running on that,” said Piastri.

“There's always things you can learn in conditions like that, so I still thought it was useful, even if it's maybe not going to be useful for the next couple of days.”

Pushed on his initial impression of the new parts, the nine-time race winner explained: “I think it's an improvement. Obviously, in these kinds of conditions, it's very tough to know exactly what it's like. But things seemed good, so hopefully it's the same in the dry.”

Piastri also insisted that his grid penalty will not have much of an impact on his approach to Friday’s Qualifying.

“It's only 10 places, so obviously the higher up I can start, the better it is still,” he conceded. “It doesn't really change that much for Qualifying. I think it's going to be an interesting Q3 session for sure, so, for me, that doesn't really change much.”

Randy Singh, Racing Director at McLaren, admitted that the conditions had made the day “tricky”, with the team taking the decision not to run the new floor that they had brought to Las Vegas due to the level of risk posed.

Singh added that the squad hope to run the update on Friday, adding: “Tomorrow's programme will be pretty condensed because we'll have three sets of tyres as well for FP3, because both sessions today were wet, so there'll be a lot to get through.

“No one's done any high-fuel running, and then we need to get ready for Qualifying as well so it will be compressed tomorrow. Certainly on the power unit side, so far all we understand is that everything's as expected, and there'll be a lot of analysis done tonight.”

Quizzed on whether McLaren can be in the fight for pole position, Singh responded: “Just really hard to say. I think the top four teams will be the same as before. It will remain tight at the front.

“Whoever does a good job with the limited running might get a bit of a better performance in Qualifying and the race. So we're trying to do our best to make the most of it, but it's too early to say at the moment.”

title: Russell beats Gasly and Leclerc to top spot in wet FP2
excerpt:
George Russell claimed top spot in Free Practice 2 ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the Mercedes driver beating Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Russell posted a 1m 47.272s at the very end of the one-hour session, which was wet throughout, leaving the Briton 0.071s clear of Gasly, with Leclerc just over three tenths back.

With no competitive lap times set during a substantially wet FP1, drivers and teams were keen to make up for a lack of running around the street circuit, which remained damp once the session got underway at 2000 local time.

Several drivers ventured out in the opening minutes on the wet Pirelli tyre, with Oscar Piastri immediately reporting over the radio that intermediate tyres might not be far away.

The McLaren man became the first driver to post a time on Thursday with a 2m 02.786s, as a flurry of names began to appear on the leaderboard and lap times began to tumble.

Fernando Alonso became the first driver to exceed the limits of grip, running deep at Turn 5 and almost nudging the barrier with the front of his Aston Martin before recovering unharmed, as Lando Norris also ran deep at Turn 14 before rejoining.

The McLaren driver and former World Champion was the first to put on a set of intermediate tyres just after the 15-minute mark as a dry line began to emerge, with Piastri having lowered the benchmark down to a 1m 55.469s.

Norris immediately jumped to the top of the times with a 1m 54.615s, the Briton going even quicker on a 1m 52.432s next time around as only team mate Piastri made the switch to the green-walled tyre.

Despite running deep at Turn 1 and Turn 7, Norris continued to set the pace approaching the halfway point, lowering the best time down to a 1m 50.930s as other drivers gradually moved across to the intermediate tyre.

Leclerc became the first driver to dip below the 1m 50s barrier, posting a 1m 49.166s and reporting "I think it's probably close to slick tyres" with 20 minutes remaining, as he set a 1m 48.473s with his next lap.

Isack Hadjar moved his Red Bull briefly to the top with a 1m 48.407s, before Leclerc usurped him with a 1m 47.605s as lap times continued to drop.

With just over 10 minutes remaining a short red flag was shown to retrieve debris heading into the final corner, the offending pieces of plastic having been blown onto the circuit.

Running resumed with just six minutes remaining, prompting a flurry of cars to appear at the end of the pit lane as the light turned green and all drivers continued to use the intermediate tyre.

Hadjar was on course to go fastest before being blocked by Ollie Bearman's Haas in the final corners, with Russell jumping to the top of the times on a 1m 47.272s as the chequered flag came out.

The Briton was fastest from Gasly's Alpine, who also improved at the very end, from Leclerc, Hadjar and Piastri, with Hamilton, Norris, Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes), the second Alpine of Franco Colapinto and Alonso completing the top 10.

Lance Stroll's Aston Martin was P11 from Alex Albon (Williams) and Max Verstappen, the Red Bull driver only setting a time in the final minutes and reporting of problems with his car.

Sergio Perez was P14 for Cadillac, from Bearman, the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, the second Williams of Carlos Sainz, the Audis of Nick Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto, Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) and Rafael Camara's Haas.

title: Antonelli, Bearman and Stroll set for penalties in Las Vegas
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli, Ollie Bearman and Lance Stroll are all set to receive grid penalties at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after each exceeding their allocation for certain power unit components.

Antonelli’s Mercedes has been fitted with a new internal combustion engine (ICE), his sixth of the season – surpassing the permitted number of four. The Italian previously served an engine penalty during his home event at Monza, leading to a memorable recovery drive from P19 to victory.

While the World Champion’s car will also run a new turbocharger and exhaust set, these are within the allocated number so do not incur a penalty.

Elsewhere Bearman’s Haas has taken on a fifth ICE, turbocharger, exhaust and motor generator unit-kinetic (MGU-K) of the season to exceed the permitted amount for each, along with a new power unit ancillary component (PU-ANC).

Over at Aston Martin, Stroll’s AMR26 is running a ninth energy store unit (ES) and eighth control electronics unit (PU-CE), going beyond the allocated three for each in a campaign.

As per the regulations, the first time the allocation of any power unit element is exceeded, a 10-place grid penalty will be applied, with the second time this occurs (and so on) resulting in a five-place grid drop – all penalties at the same event applying in a cumulative manner.

If a driver incurs a penalty exceeding 15 grid places, they will be required to start the race at the back of the field regardless.

This means that Antonelli will serve a five-place penalty, with Stroll set for a 10-place drop and Bearman due to start from the back of the grid.

Others already confirmed to receive penalties in Las Vegas include Oscar Piastri and Carlos Sainz, who will both drop 10 grid positions.

title: Mercedes’ first female junior Fluxa Cross on her F1 ACADEMY debut
excerpt:
Luna Fluxa Cross has been one of the most talked about up-and-coming female drivers for the past few years. Now the Mercedes junior is preparing for the biggest stage of her career so far as she makes her F1 ACADEMY debut on the streets of Las Vegas.

Fluxa Cross is competing as the Wild Card entry for Round 6, a one-off appearance created to strengthen the talent pool in the regions where the all-female series races.

Competing in the Spanish F4 Championship this season, the 16-year-old faces a steep learning curve. She needs to adapt to a new car, a new team in Hitech and new tyres alongside racing on a street circuit for the first time. On top of that comes the jet lag that challenges every driver on an overseas round.

“It feels amazing,” she said. “I'm really grateful to be the last Wild Card of the season, especially here in Vegas. It's a very nice track and my first street circuit, so I'm looking forward to getting the weekend started.

“It’s going to be about learning and let's see if we can extract the most out of it. I've done some gym sessions and of course [I have a] jet lag plan to get used to all the times. I have everything all ready, so it's very exciting and I'm very looking forward to getting out on track.”

Mercedes spotted Fluxa Cross’ talent long before this weekend. Back in 2022, aged just 11, she became the first female driver to join the Mercedes-AMG F1 Junior Programme. She is now the longest-standing junior in their roster.

Gwen Lagrue has headed the programme since 2016 — he leaves to become Director of the Red Bull Junior Programme in 2027 — and has scouted many of motorsport's brightest stars, not least Formula 1 World Champion Kimi Antonelli and eight-time Grand Prix winner George Russell.

The Silver Arrows’ faith in the Spaniard has proved well-deserved. Fluxa Cross was chosen as part of the inaugural karting cohort for F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE in the Champions of the Future Academy Program International Series in 2024. Seizing the opportunity, she dominated the season. She became the first female winner of an FIA international championship since 1966 and claimed the OK-N Senior title by 125 points.

Mercedes’ support has continued to strengthen since she moved to single-seaters this season, and Fluxa Cross stressed the pivotal role the team has played in getting her to this milestone moment.

“It's been a very long journey with them which I'm very grateful for,” she noted. “It feels like I’m part of a family. They've helped me a lot not only trackside but also in training and nutrition.

F1 ACADEMY announces 2027 calendar

“Also outside of track, [Mercedes are] helping me keeping my head in the right mindset and knowing how to approach every weekend. I think they have a really big role in my journey and my career.”

The Wild Card initiative has become a key component of the series’ driver market and a pathway for the next generation of talent. Since its introduction in 2024, nine Wild Cards have earned a full-time seat the following season, including 2026 Champion Alisha Palmowski. Meanwhile, Payton Westcott earned her spot with Mercedes after an impressive debut in Las Vegas last year.

This season, Chiara Battig set a high bar, becoming the first Wild Card driver to achieve a pole position and a podium in Silverstone. However, the Red Bull Junior has also been the only Wild Card entry to score points in 2026.

Looking to add herself to that list, Fluxa Cross isn’t oblivious to what a successful weekend could mean for her future but is choosing to focus on the challenge in front of her rather than what others think she’s capable of.

Asked if points were her target this weekend, she responded jokingly: “Yeah of course, that’s a silly question (laughs).

“I think it's better to go without expectations and see how the weekend plays out. Of course, I’m a Wild Card, so it's my first round in this series. Getting to learn everything and getting up to terms, it’s going to be more tricky for me, but I'm looking forward the challenge and let's see how it plays out.”

She added: “It's very crucial that I show what I'm capable of as it's a good opportunity for a seat next year.

"Also on the other hand, it's just to enjoy it. I do the sport to enjoy it and because that's where I get the results. I'll just go out there with a clear mind and just drive as I know how to.”

title: What to watch out for in the F1 ACADEMY season finale
excerpt:
The bright lights of the Las Vegas Strip play host to the final round of what has been an intense campaign. While some drivers will be looking ahead to their next challenge, others are eager to prove they deserve a seat for next year. Here’s everything you’ll want to keep an eye on this weekend…

Who will end PREMA'S teams' title reign?

PREMA Racing have secured all three teams’ titles since the all-female series’ inaugural season back in 2023, but the Italian squad’s reign is about to come to an end.

After helping Alisha Palmowski seize the drivers’ title, Campos Racing are on the verge of doing the double for the first time. They hold a 44-point advantage over MP Motorsport and an 80-point lead over Rodin Motorsport, with a maximum of 86 points left to play for.

However, their grip on the top spot has slowly slipped over the past two rounds, having stood at 100 points after Silverstone. Alpine’s Nina Gademan and Alba Larsen have been crucial to MP’s resurgence, with the pair claiming a combined eight podiums in the past five races.

Overcoming that gap at the final hurdle won’t be easy, particularly at a track Campos took a 1-2 finish at last year with Chloe Chambers and Palmowski. However, the streets of Las Vegas are nothing if not unpredictable.

Mercedes' first female junior makes her debut

Luna Fluxa Cross made history back in 2022 when she became the first female driver to join the Mercedes-AMG F1 Junior Programme aged just 11. Now the 16-year-old prepares to make her F1 ACADEMY debut, racing on a street circuit for the first time as the Las Vegas Wild Card driver.

Fans of the series will already be familiar with Fluxa Cross after she was selected as F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE karter for the Champions of the Future Academy Program International Series in 2024. The Spaniard went on to dominate the season, becoming the first female winner of an FIA international championship since 1966.

This season saw her graduate to single-seaters, scoring a podium in the Eurocup-4 Spanish Winter Championship at Portimao and points in the F4 Spanish Championship, alongside appearing in this year’s F1 ACADEMY Rookie Test.

Only one Wild Card driver has claimed points this season, with Chiara Battig’s history-making pole position and podium at Silverstone. Unlike the Red Bull Junior, Fluxa Cross hasn’t had the chance to race at Las Vegas beforehand, but the F1 ACADEMY grid and Mercedes will be watching to see what results she can deliver.

Top rookie battle goes down to the wire

There’s another fight that’s also yet to be decided, as three drivers face off in the battle to be the rookie of the year.

It’s a full circle moment for Payton Westcott, who made her series debut on these same streets last year. Since then, the Mercedes driver has achieved her maiden win in Zandvoort, alongside three further podium finishes. Currently fifth in the overall standings, she leads the rookie group by 18 points ahead of PREMA Racing team mate, Natalia Granada.

Granada has experienced a resurgence of her own, taking home her second podium of the season in Austin — her first since the Sephora driver’s debut race in Shanghai.

Campos’ Megan Bruce is also in the hunt but has lost some ground to the pair since leading the rookie fight after round 2 in Montreal, sitting a further six points behind Granada.

The 2027 grid is already taking shape

Although the 2026 season isn’t quite over yet, plans are already beginning to be finalised for next season.

Following a rule change announced last year, drivers can now be granted a third campaign if their performance indicates strong potential for continued growth. Two drivers have already benefitted from this, with Ferrari locking in Larsen and Audi continuing with Emma Felbermayr for 2027.

Of the rookie cohort, only Jade Jacquet’s seat is secured. After scoring her first points in Austin and following that up with a career-best finish of P4, Williams have stuck with the French F4 race winner for another year.

Meanwhile, champion Palmowski will be looking ahead to new pastures as she graduates to the Formula Regional European Championship with Rodin Motorsport and joins the Red Bull Junior Team.

For the rest of the field, this is their last chance to prove to the F1 teams and partners that they deserve anotherchance, or to show other series that they’ve got the talent to take that next step up in their racing journeys.

title: Komatsu insists there is 'no doubt' over Bearman’s Haas seat
excerpt:
Confirmation of Valtteri Bottas at Cadillac leaves just one 2027 Formula 1 seat with a question mark over it as Ollie Bearman has yet to sign a new contract with Haas.

On Wednesday in Las Vegas the Englishman made clear his frustration as negotiations continue to drag on.

The good news is that on the Haas side there are no doubts, as Team Principal Ayao Komatsu made clear in Las Vegas when asked if the uncertainty might affect Bearman’s motivation.

“I don't think he needs motivation,” said Komatsu. “He's very, very motivated. I think you can see that week in, week out. That's not an issue at all. But yeah, the contract, it just takes some time to align everyone, finalise everything.

“But everybody's aligned. Ollie wants to drive for us; we want Ollie in the car. So there's no doubt it's going to happen. It's just unfortunate that it's taking a long time – but it's going to happen.”

Komatsu wouldn’t be drawn on Ferrari’s role in the delay, with the Briton part of their junior setup.

“Again, like I said, it's just there's many parties involved," the Haas boss continued. "I don't want to go into detail, but there's no doubt he's going to be in the car next year. It will happen.”

Regarding Bearman’s obvious frustration he added: “Obviously as a driver, you want the contract wrapped up much earlier than this. So yes, it's understandable.”

Meanwhile, on the other side of the Haas garage, Las Vegas will be another weekend of learning for Rafael Camara. The Brazilian youngster won’t face the same sort of home race pressures that he had at Interlagos, and he has also had more time to prepare, with sim sessions back in Europe. Nevertheless it is not an easy venue for a rookie.

“Obviously we threw him into the most difficult weekend in Brazil,” Komatsu admitted.

“Considering everything, I thought he coped really, really well, and then the speed he's shown was pretty impressive.

“So here it's going to be whole new challenge – street circuit, different downforce level, and then the grip this circuit offers is very low. On top of that one, it's even colder than last year. So getting the tyres to work will be a huge challenge. On top of that, we might have rain.

“I don't think for a debut race in Brazil he could have had more difficult race, or weekend. He coped very well. So no doubt he will cope very well [here]. But again, this will be another big challenge.”

title: Max Verstappen hands Kimi Antonelli 'living in a cloud' warning after F1 title glory
excerpt:
Max Verstappen knows exactly what it is like to become an F1 world champion.

Max Verstappen has warned Kimi Antonelli against "living in a cloud" after the Mercedes driver became the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, while insisting the Italian's inner circle will keep him grounded.

Antonelli sealed the 2026 title with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix, a result that made him champion at 20 years and 68 days old and smashed Sebastian Vettel's previous record by more than three years.

The 20-year-old also became the first Italian to win the drivers' title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

Verstappen, who won the Mexico City GP on the day his title rival was crowned, was asked by talkSPORT whether he was pleased for Antonelli or already focused on beating him in 2027.

"Well, it definitely helped because I actually won the race, right?" the four-time champion said. "But no, he's a great kid.

"He has a great family around him, and that's why what he has achieved this year is really remarkable. And that's why you can be very proud of what he has achieved. When you're just a nice, genuine person, right?

"That is something that I really respect, and that's why I think also you can really enjoy the moment. I know myself how that felt. The first time that you've won a championship is very emotional, and then when you have your family around to celebrate it as well, yeah, it is something really, really special."

Max Verstappen boasts full confidence in Kimi Antonelli inner-circle

Across his junior career and opening two years in F1, Antonelli has kept his family incredibly case, especially his father.

Pressed on whether he had any advice for Antonelli now that the title is in the bag, Verstappen pointed to the people surrounding the young Italian as the key safeguard against complacency.

"I think it also just depends a little bit on the people around you, right? That keep you with two feet on the ground," the Red Bull driver said. "I know that he has that, and I think that is so important because it was very easy to, well, kind of like start flying now.

"You know, be living in a cloud, but he has the right people around him to keep him grounded and wanting more."

"He's already said it himself, it's great to win one, but he wants to win more, he wants to keep winning. I think that's his mindset as well.

"Yeah, like I said, it's very important to have the right people around you to tell you still, when it's not good or when you have done something wrong, you keep trying to develop yourself."

title: F1 team bosses react as V8 engine return 'agreement' is reached
excerpt:
F1's next power unit regulations look set to come into play in 2030 as a return to V8 engines is on the horizon.

A number of F1 teams have publicly voiced their support for the return of V8 engines as part of the sport's next cycle of technical regulations.

Following the launch of the new 2026 power unit regulations, discussions quickly shifted to what would come next.

The FIA raised the possibility of using V8 engines once again, which were last used in 2013 before the shift to V6 hybrid power units.

Earlier this week, a major meeting was held between the FIA, F1 and its teams where a common agreement was reached to bring back the V8s in just over three years' time.

"There's an agreement in principle," McLaren CEO Zak Brown told media including RacingNews365.

"Everyone is very excited. Now it's about dotting the i's and crossing the t's.

"If you look at what the FIA has done, they've announced full-time stewards, so they are very proactive; they move quick, they do what they say they're going to do.

"The sport has never been healthier, the competition is amazing. I've got a lot of confidence in the future of the sport. Where it is today is great.

"I'm excited for the new engines, everyone will be. But there's a lot more also going on to continue to evolve the sport.

"Between the FIA and F1 they're doing a great job."

[Article continues below]

© XPB Images

Alpine, Cadillac back V8 engine return

Brown's comment was mirrored by Alpine boss Flavio Briatore, who insisted the engine is what the fans want to see.

"We have an agreement, basically," he said. "It is not signed, but it looks everybody is agreed [for] 2030 [to have] V8s.

"I'm very happy, it's the right way to go. We need an engine with a lot of noise, a simple engine, and we need racing with that.

"In the end, I believe what is best is for the spectator, for everybody, is a very simple engine, a lot of noise."

F1 newcomers Cadillac are preparing to become a works team as they build their own engine, with their facility opening in just under one month's time.

They are expecting to put heavy investment behind the new power unit to make it ready to run on track once the sport's new era gets underway.

"We're glad to see the series coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030," said team owner Dan Towriss.

"We're super happy with that. Our new power unit facility opens up on December 18th.

"So as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, the direction is obviously very helpful. We're excited about the direction and the crew is hard at work, getting ready."

title: George Russell draws first blood in Las Vegas following FP1 washout
excerpt:
George Russell topped FP2 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, setting his best time right at the death following a late red flag and tricky conditions in Sin City.

20 November 6:07AM

George Russell topped the timing board in FP2 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, after no one set a lap during a wet first free practice session in Sin City.

Pierre Gasly was second-quickest at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit, almost pipping the Mercedes with the final lap of nth session, with the leading Ferrari of Charles Leclerc third.

Isack Hadjar and Oscar Piastri rounded out the top five, ahead of Lewis Hamilton, whilst F1's two most recent drivers' champions, Lando Norris and Kimi Antonelli, were seventh and eighth in a session that went from wet tyres to intermediates.

The session was disrupted for a few minutes towards the end when Lance Stroll struck a plastic box lining, leaving remnants all over the circuit on the approach to the final corner.

Check out the full FP2 report for the Las Vegas Grand Prix below!

George Russell draws first blood in Las Vegas following FP1 washout

# Driver Team Time Tyre

Results are being loaded...

First half

Following a washed-out FP1 that saw no timed laps, the field — and everyone watching — will have hoped for a drier start to the second hour of running in Nevada.

Nonetheless, half the pack did emerge on track in the opening five minutes of FP1, all on the blue-walled wet Pirellis. The first three cars out, Arvid Lindblad, Oscar Piastri and Liam Lawson, had all declined to leave the pits at all during the opening session.

It was the McLaren driver who would cut the beam, setting the first timed lap of the weekend, a 2:02.786. That was soon bested by Charles Leclerc by three tenths, and then his team-mate Norris by three seconds, dipping below the two-minute mark.

Fernando Alonso had the first heart-in-mouth moment, locking up and narrowly avoiding sliding into the outside barrier at Turn 5, with the icy conditions proving treacherous, despite no rain falling at the time.

As the lap times fell further, Leclerc went quicker than the McLarens with a 1:58.0, all before Piastri brought the marker down by a second.

Norris, meanwhile, in the other MCL40, had a spin, all before going to the top of the timing board. His eventful session continued when, around the 17-minute mark, he strapped on a set of intermediates, being the first driver to do so.

Having slipped to fourth, the 2025 F1 drivers' champion was soon finding chunks of lap time, going two-and-a-half seconds quicker than anyone else with a 1:52.432, prompting others to join him.

As the session reached the halfway point, the British driver was still top, quite comfortably, with a 1:50.930. It was a second and a half faster than anyone else and impressively remained over five tenths clear of the chasing pack for well over 10 minutes before Leclerc set a new benchmark time of 1:49.166.

Second half

With just 20 minutes to go, only Max Verstappen had not tried the green-walled intermediate tyres, sitting P22 and last on the timing board without an effort to his name.

The Red Bull driver was clearly in no rush, seen standing around his garage, chatting to engineers.

Isack Hadjar, in the sister RB22, was enjoying himself out on track, despite the tricky conditions. The French driver went top with a 1:48.407, only to be usurped by Leclerc shortly after, to the tune of eight tenths of a second.

The session was red-flagged for a few minutes due to some plastic box lining on track, for which Katy Perry would almost be proud, only for it to be collected and destroyed by the Aston Martin of Stroll, denying it an American Beauty moment.

When the session resumed with little over five minutes to run, Verstappen decided to join his peers, but was not happy.

Complaining of a lack of power, his race engineer, Tom Hart, informed the Dutchman it was merely his engine coming up to temperature, to which his driver replied: "This is not normal, come on. This is not normal!"

The four-time F1 drivers' champion continued his tirade, labelling his car "not good", comparing its problems to those he experienced in the latter stages in Brazil. He finished the session P13.

Up front, the lap times tumbled, with Russell pipping Leclerc at the post, with Gasly slipping in to second for Alpine.

title: Bizarre Las Vegas GP red flag as Lance Stroll unfortunate victim
excerpt:
Second practice ahead of this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix has been red-flagged with just under 10 minutes remaining, following a bizarre incident.

A large piece of plastic blew onto the Las Vegas Strip Circuit in the final sector and was unfortunately struck by Aston Martin's Lance Stroll.

The incident ripped the plastic into several smaller pieces, triggering a red flag for the circuit to be cleaned.

Once cleaned, the session was resumed with six minutes remaining, on what remained a slippery surface but with an increasing number of dry patches.

It still saw intermediate tyres being used, with Charles Leclerc quickest when running resumed.

title: Two more F1 drivers join growing Las Vegas GP grid-penalty victim list
excerpt:
Oliver Bearman and Lance Stroll have both been handed grid penalties for the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The duo join an ever-growing list of drivers who will be demoted on the starting grid after qualifying on Saturday.

Bearman has been fitted with a new combustion engine, turbocharger and MGU-K, resulting in a 35-place grid penalty.

As per the rules, this has been automatically transferred into a back-of-the-grid demotion as it exceeds 15 places.

Stroll, who has been enduring a painful season with Aston Martin, will drop 10 places on the grid due to taking on a new energy store and control electronics.

They are the fourth and fifth drivers respectively to have grid penalties, joining Kimi Antonelli, Oscar Piastri and Carlos Sainz.

title: Cadillac outline next move for shunned Colton Herta
excerpt:
You have to wonder where Colton Herta will now end up.

Cadillac has confirmed it is still working on what comes next for Colton Herta after the American was shunned for a 2027 F1 race seat.

Herta's hopes of an immediate promotion were ended on Thursday when Cadillac confirmed Valtteri Bottas alongside Sergio Pérez for next season, despite him recently acquiring his FIA super licence.

Asked what the plan is for Herta going forward, Cadillac team principal Marcin Budkowski said the team is weighing up its options.

"We are discussing that," Budkowski told Sky Sports F1. "First, we needed to confirm our race drivers. We have done that now, and we're looking at what the plan is in terms of reserve, but also in terms of the longer plan for the drivers.

"So, we're talking to Colton and his management for next year and the following years.

"The ambition of this team is to have an American driver at some point in the car. It needs to be the right driver, the right timing, and the right combination."

[Article continues below]

Budkowski - 'More difficult than he anticipated'

Budkowski also addressed the difficulties Herta faced adapting to European machinery and circuits in his rookie F2 campaign, acknowledging it had not gone as smoothly as hoped.

"He's been racing in F2 this year," said Budkowski. "It's been a difficult season, probably more difficult than he had anticipated or everybody had anticipated. There are a lot of factors there, and I'm not going to get into the details of them.

"We've given him six FP1 sessions in the end; one of them was compromised by reliability issues, but let's say five counted.

"That gave him some mileage in the car. It gave him some experience of circuits where he hadn't raced before, and he got that super licence.

"There are objectives we gave ourselves. He's race-ready in terms of mileage and in terms of super licence, and then we're looking at what the future holds for us with him."

title: Las Vegas GP suffers wet-weather disaster as 'risk not worth the reward'
excerpt:
Persistent rain blighted the opening practice session for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with not a single timed lap posted.

Fans in the grandstands around the city circuit will have been left frustrated by the fact that only 20 exploratory laps were recorded over the hour-long session. Five drivers did not even leave the garage.

As McLaren CEO Zak Brown noted, with Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri amongst those who stayed dry, the "risk was not worth the reward" of venturing out in case one of his team's cars ended up in a wall.

Notably, with conditions set to improve for FP2, and with the forecast for the weekend being cool and dry, there was naturally little point in taking to a wet track given any data would be irrelevant for the rest of the event.

[Article continues below]

Five F1 drivers don't bother

In the build-up to the session, light rain fell before gradually increasing as the clock ticked down to the start.

By the time the session commenced, the streets of Las Vegas were sodden, creating treacherous conditions.

It was almost five minutes before a car took to the track, with Cadillac's Sergio Perez venturing out on full wet Pirellis.

Reserves in Ferrari's Dino Beganovic and Aston Martin's Jak Crawford, replacing Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso respectively, tiptoed their way around the wet track, with standing water in many places, as steady rain continued to fall.

It was then the turn of Williams' duo Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz, and incoming champion Kimi Antonelli in his Mercedes, to try a lap. Antonelli complained of "aquaplaning everywhere" before being told to box.

Red Bull pair Isack Hadjar and Max Verstappen, along with Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, followed suit, all for one lap as nobody opted for a timed lap, before the turn of Charles Leclerc in his Ferrari and the second Audi of Nico Hulkenberg.

Camara was one of three drivers who 'enjoyed' a second lap, before Mercedes' George Russell, with five minutes remaining, cast his eye over the circuit. Alpine pair Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto were the last to take to the track late on in a disappointing session for the fans.

Alongside Norris and Piastri, Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll were the only drivers not to bother.

title: F1 announces key partnership as global giant ends 20-year absence
excerpt:
Formula 1 has announced American sportswear giant Nike as its new apparel and uniform supplier ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The announcement marks the global giant's return to F1 for the first time in two decades, as Nike taps into the sport's increasingly younger audience. It will join as an official partner from 2027.

Nike will deliver capsule collections spanning footwear, apparel, and accessories, alongside performance innovations and race-weekend experiences for fans.

Fans will get their first look at what is on offer with a limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection on November 20 at the F1 Hub and Nike Las Vegas stores.

Nike will additionally become official partner and official sporting apparel partner of F1 Academy.

Stefano Domenicali, F1 president and CEO, said of the deal: "Formula 1 and Nike are two of the world's most iconic brands, united by a relentless drive to innovate, perform at the highest level, and inspire people to push beyond what is possible.

"Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth, reaching hundreds of millions of fans and engaging one of the most passionate, diverse and dynamic communities in sport.

"Nike's unique ability to sit at the intersection of sport, culture and inspiration makes them the ideal partner as we enter our next chapter."

"This partnership is a powerful reflection of Formula 1's scale, ambition and global momentum. Together, we have an extraordinary opportunity to redefine how fans connect with our sport, create lasting impact across both Formula 1 and F1 Academy and inspire the next generation of racers, creators and innovators around the world.

"This is far more than a commercial partnership; it is the coming together of two brands that shape culture, challenge convention and set new standards of excellence. We are only at the start of what we can achieve together, and the possibilities ahead are truly limitless."

Nike president and CEO Elliott Hill said the two organisations share the same competitive outlook.

"Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate," he said. "That's an athlete mindset, and it's one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world.”

title: Third Formula 1 driver hit with Las Vegas Grand Prix grid penalty
excerpt:
Carlos Sainz will start the Las Vegas Grand Prix with a 10-place grid penalty after Williams fitted a fifth turbocharger to his car for the weekend.

The new component is an upgraded turbocharger specification developed by Mercedes High Performance Powertrains under the FIA's Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities mechanism, granted after the manufacturer's internal combustion engine was found to be running between two and four per cent behind the benchmark power unit.

Mercedes made the upgraded part available to its works team and customers, including Williams and McLaren, with its on-track debut planned for Las Vegas.

A Williams spokesperson confirmed that both Sainz and team-mate Alex Albon would take the new specification.

"Alex and Carlos will both run the ADUO-enabled turbo specification this weekend," the spokesperson said.

"Carlos will take a 10-place grid penalty, as it will be his fifth turbocharger and exceeds the permitted annual allocation."

Albon avoids a penalty as the new unit falls within his own season allowance.

Elsewhere on the grid, Mercedes customer Kimi Antonelli faces a five-place drop after taking a sixth engine, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri will also serve a 10-place penalty for taking a fifth ICE.

title: FIA to introduce full-time stewards for F1 from 2027
excerpt:
This is a major step change for the FIA and Formula 1

The FIA has confirmed it will appoint full-time stewards to Formula 1 for the first time, beginning a phased rollout from the 2027 season.

The governing body says the move is designed to bring greater consistency and dedication to race officiating at the highest level of the sport.

A small number of full-time stewards will be recruited during the 2027 campaign, with the FIA aiming to expand that group further for the 2028 season and beyond.

Existing FIA stewards will not be replaced. They will continue working alongside the new recruits as part of a mixed roster of full-time and part-time officials for the foreseeable future.

Driver stewards will keep their role at each event, with the federation recognising the specialist knowledge they bring.

The FIA has now launched a recruitment drive for experienced international stewards to form the first generation of full-time officials, who will work alongside its existing pool of qualified stewards.

Building towards a bigger department

The federation says the dedicated full-time structure will provide continuity and expertise, supporting its ongoing review of sporting regulations and stewarding guidelines.

It is also expected to allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making across race weekends.

Beyond the grands prix themselves, the FIA says the new stewards will have increased capacity to spot emerging trends and flag areas requiring regulatory clarification, feeding into the evolution of the sporting regulations.

They will also be tasked with training and mentoring future generations of FIA officials, contributing to the FIA High Performance Programme and pushing for greater harmonisation across the federation's championships.

[Article continues below]

The plan is for the department to grow in the coming years to between 12 and 15 full-time stewards, a structure that would eventually extend support to other FIA single-seater championships.

The move is the latest step in a restructuring of officiating at the top of motorsport that began under FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem at the start of his mandate, following a reorganisation of Race Control in 2022, the creation of the FIA Officials department, and sustained investment in FIA Systems Operations.

Last month, the FIA opened an all-new Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill in the UK, a facility built to maintain the highest standards of race management.

The federation says the financial turnaround under Ben Sulayem's leadership has made the stewarding programme possible, allowing it to reinvest in its core sporting responsibilities.

Ben Sulayem said the appointment of full-time stewards reflects the FIA's commitment to decision-making standards in the sport.

"This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport," said Ben Sulayem.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship; it is also an investment in the future of our sport."

"Following the milestone opening of the new FIA Remote Operations Centre and strengthening of officiating development through initiatives such as the FIA High Performance Programme, this development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships."

title: Sergio Perez welcomes Cadillac 'distraction' end as 2027 lineup confirmed
excerpt:
Sergio Perez has welcomed the end of a lingering distraction after Cadillac confirmed its 2027 driver lineup, with Valtteri Bottas set to remain his teammate following weeks of speculation that linked the Finn's seat to Colton Herta.

Cadillac confirmed on Wednesday that it had exercised its contract option to keep Bottas for a second season, ending uncertainty that had built up after Perez himself was signed to an extension earlier in the year while Bottas's deal contained only a team option rather than a guaranteed drive.

Herta had picked up the FIA superlicence points required to race in Formula 1 through practice outings in Austin, Mexico City and Sao Paulo, fuelling talk that the American, backed by TWG Motorsports, could be fast-tracked into the second Cadillac seat for the team's second year on the grid.

Cadillac instead opted for continuity, pointing to Bottas's experience as crucial to resolving the reliability problems, including recurring brake cooling and suspension issues, that hampered the American outfit's debut campaign.

Asked how happy he is to continue with Bottas, Perez told select media, including RacingNews365: "Ah, very. I think I work well with Valtteri. I think he brings a lot of speed, a lot of experience to the team, and I think at this stage it's crucial.

"I've always said, I think the team has much more important things to focus on than drivers for now. So, yeah, happy in that regard. Now we can take that distraction out of our way and make sure that operationally we can make good stops, can do good things, because the last few races operationally have been weak."

Sergio Perez 'happy' for Valtteri Bottas partnership continuation

Perez also revealed he had been mindful of the pressure the rumours placed on his teammate throughout the process.

Discussing whether he had asked Bottas how he felt during the contract speculation, Perez said:

"I mean, obviously, I was aware of the situation, and it's not easy as a teammate to know what's fully going on, and all you can do is just support and, yeah, hope for the best for your teammate. You know that you are spending a lot of time with him, and I'm happy, really, he's staying."

title: Oscar Piastri confirms 'interim' arrangement after surprise Mark Webber exit
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri has had his say over the surprise split with Mark and Ann Webber from his management team.

Oscar Piastri has confirmed that he is currently working with an "interim" management set-up after the surprise exits of Mark and Ann Webber.

It was announced on the Monday following the Sao Paulo Grand Prix that Piastri would split with the Webbers with immediate effect, with the Webbers having guided Piastri up from the junior categories to F1, where he made his debut in 2023.

Despite the odd timing of the announcement, Piastri has explained that there is not a ready-to-go replacement for the Webbers, and that for the time being, he is working with an "interim" management set-up.

"I don't have anyone confirmed," Piastri replied when asked by RacingNews365 if he was going to take his time to assess the options around him.

"I've obviously got an interim set-up at the moment, but nothing is set in stone for the future.

"I'll define that in due course."

[Article continues below]

Piastri on Webber exit

Turning to the Webbers, Piastri spoke of the "massive role" they had played in bringing him into F1 after a stellar junior career, including back-to-back titles in FIA F2 and FIA F3.

"They played a massive role in my career and getting to this point - the end of my junior career and the start of my F1 career.

"The support at the track and behind the scenes was incredibly valuable, and I think now is the appropriate time to go our separate ways and do new things.

"I haven't got anything set in stone at the moment. I am still looking at what the future looks like, for the team around me."

title: Liam Lawson admits to 'strange' feeling despite landing new F1 contract
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has explained the "strange" feeling he holds despite landing a 2027 Racing Bulls F1 contract before the end of the season.

Weeks of speculation ended last week when it was formally announced that Lawson, who is a strong ninth in the championship with 89 points and the highest-placed non-Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull, or McLaren driver, would be kept on for 2027.

There had been serious doubt about his seat with Red Bull evaluating F2 protege Nikola Tsolov for potential promotion, but the Bulgarian must make do with a third and reserve driver role at both Red Bull and Racing Bulls in 2027.

For New Zealander Lawson, knowing his future before the end of the season is something he is unaccustomed to, as he explained.

"It's obviously a good feeling, a little bit of relief for me. It's a little bit strange, just because I've actually not really done races or finished the season knowing a little bit early," Lawson told media, including RacingNews365.

"I feel like it is more normal to do that, but for us at least, it hasn't been in the past, so it's a little bit of a strange feeling, but it's obviously nice.

"And for me, I'll try and enjoy the last few races even more. I mean, I honestly have enjoyed racing a lot this year, especially the second half, despite everything going on in the background.

"I'm just going to try and keep that rolling through the last couple of races."

[Article continues below]

Lawson doubt

When then asked if there was a moment he feared he would not get the nod for 2027, Lawson conceded to having doubts at times.

"I don't think so, not really. I mean, if I look back to last year, I feel like I was thinking about it a lot, and it was definitely... You have a lot of doubts always, especially when things aren't going well," he said.

"But I feel like for us this year, things have been just quite strong across the board. Especially since the summer break; things have been really, really good for us as a team. We've had a strong car across all the tracks, and I feel like we've executed mostly each weekend.

"So I didn't feel like I struggled to find a reason why, but obviously you think about it, and it's talked about a lot. But I feel like, more than anything, I just tried to remove that sort of thought process from my mind as much as I could and just try to focus and enjoy driving the car.

"And I felt like we were able to do that."

title: Kimi Antonelli explains reason to fear Red Bull in Las Vegas 'outlier'
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has outlined why Red Bull will be such a formidable challenge at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Kimi Antonelli expects Red Bull to be Mercedes' main rival at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where the long straights play to the strengths of its combustion engine and low-drag 'Macarena' rear wing.

The teams' two power units have different strengths. Red Bull has held the advantage on internal combustion engine performance in the FIA's ADUO assessments this season, a significant achievement in what is its first campaign as a power unit manufacturer.

But Antonelli also highlighted how Mercedes has the edge in how efficiently it managed energy from the battery, a particular challenge over the lap in Las Vegas, which is a power-sensitive circuit.

Nonetheless, the F1 drivers' champion expects the RB22 to be a formidable challenge in Sin City.

"Red Bull is going to be very strong this weekend," Antonelli told media, including RacingNews365.

"However, I think we're the only one who has a set of wings that have slightly lower downforce, so a bit less draggy. So it's gonna be interesting. Let's see if we're gonna use it here.

"But definitely, it's gonna be very interesting. Our power unit has been very strong on the electrical side.

"Obviously, also on the combustion side, but the electrical side has been very strong. I think we're probably the most efficient ones in terms of electrical power and efficiency.

"However, Red Bull as well; they have a very strong power unit, and their car is very efficient on the straight, especially with the Macarena wing they have. So, I think it's gonna be very interesting."

[Article continues below]

Why Las Vegas is an 'outlier'

The cold will make it difficult for drivers to get their tyres up to temperature, and Antonelli expects the grip on the street circuit to change considerably between the first two practice sessions.

It will be a critical factor once qualifying and the 50-lap race come around, with temperatures expected to start around 12 degrees Celsius for both sessions before cooling further.

"It's gonna be one of those races that is a bit of an outlier because, again, it's very difficult on energy," Antonelli added. "But it's going to be so cold, so having the tyres at the right temperature is going to be key. So let's see.

"And also, track evolution is gonna be massive. I think FP1 is gonna be drifting, and then maybe FP2 is gonna be back to normal driving.

"I think our main competitor will be Red Bull this weekend, probably McLaren as well. Let's see also Ferrari, how they're going to do."
